newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO soften as Iraqi oil made its debut.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO soften as Iraqi oil made its debut.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Tuesday were under pressure as Iraqi oil made its debut in the oil market, traders said.
Talks of the resumption of Iraq oil took centrestage, they said. Prices of fuel oil, tracked the losses in crude, fell steadily.

Offers were first heard at $123 per tonne for end December loading supplies but the same offer by a major gradually ease to $120.50 after finding no buyers. Chinese demand were expected to stem the slide in prices, traders said.
South Korean supplies in December were sold out with two cargoes heard available in January.
In the swaps market, December was down at $119.75/$120.75, lower from Monday's quotes of $121.50/$122.
